initiatives.title: Iceberg Performance and Metadata Optimization
initiatives.summary: A comprehensive initiative addressing Iceberg's performance bottlenecks and metadata efficiency through multiple complementary improvements: parallel task execution for small file handling, transaction commit optimization, REST API enhancements for batch operations, metadata format improvements (delta-encoded schemas, v4 manifest design), and cost-based optimizer statistics. The work spans Spark reader improvements, REST catalog federation, and metadata storage reduction.
key_points: Parallel/asynchronous task execution in Spark readers to improve small file workload performance
Transaction commit bottleneck mitigation through REST batch endpoints and multi-statement transactions
Metadata bloat reduction via delta-encoded schemas, compact JSON formatting, and v4 manifest design with deletion vectors
Cost-based optimizer improvements through manifest-level statistics and partial metadata loading
REST API enhancements including bulk object lookup, credential refresh, and server-side metadata tables

initiatives.title: Iceberg Specification and Format Evolution
initiatives.summary: A comprehensive initiative to evolve Iceberg's table specification and format across multiple versions (V3/V4), addressing deletion strategies, metadata enhancements, REST catalog improvements, and new features like materialized views and row lineage. The work involves clarifying existing spec ambiguities, deprecating legacy patterns, and implementing performance improvements while maintaining backward compatibility.
key_points: Advancing deletion handling: transitioning from equality deletes to deletion vectors (DVs) and position deletes, with proposals to deprecate equality deletes and improve position delete efficiency

Specification clarifications and V3 finalization: resolving ambiguities around identifier uniqueness, temporal calendars, identity partitions, and time travel semantics with planned RC release for testing
Metadata and feature enhancements: adding row lineage, table labels, variant shredding support, materialized views, and optional table name persistence to improve operational capabilities
REST Catalog restructuring: proposing dedicated repository with phased improvements (v1/v2) and reference implementation for better specification management
Format evolution: supporting relative paths, secondary indexing, and improved CDC support through RowId-based deletion mechanisms

initiatives.title: Iceberg Specification and API Evolution
initiatives.summary: A comprehensive initiative to modernize Apache Iceberg's specification, APIs, and implementations through deprecations, standardization, and forward compatibility improvements. The effort spans multiple areas including file format APIs, snapshot management, language bindings, and connector updates, with several proposals in voting stages and active implementation work.
key_points: File Format API proposal achieving unified interface with incremental merge strategy and FileAppenderFactory deprecation
Snapshot management improvements including race condition fixes, retention policies, and metadata standardization
Language binding expansion through C FFI, Ruby bindings, and C++ development acceleration using iceberg-rust
Specification clarifications for optional fields, snapshot summaries, and implementation notes with forward compatibility considerations
Deprecation of legacy components (Spark 3.3/3.4, HadoopTableOperations, position deletes with row data) to streamline maintenance

Deprecation and removal of older Spark versions (3.2) to reduce maintenance burden and ensure feature parity across supported versions

Seeks alignment on naming and coordination strategy across Java, Python, Go, and Rust implementations

Specification clarifications and enhancements including encryption, default values, and partition stats
Community voting process with some vetoed RCs requiring iteration before successful passage

initiatives.title: Add ROUND_ROBIN DistributionMode to core API
initiatives.summary: Proposal to add a new ROUND_ROBIN value to the core DistributionMode enum to distinguish between true no-redistribution (NONE) and round-robin distribution across writers. This change aims to eliminate serdes and shuffle overhead in Flink's DynamicIcebergSink by enabling operator chaining, with consensus from Flink committers and mapping to Spark's unspecified distribution.
key_points: Current NONE mode in DynamicIcebergSink performs round-robin distribution, inconsistent with regular IcebergSink behavior
Adding ROUND_ROBIN mode would allow NONE to mean true no-redistribution, enabling operator chaining and eliminating serdes/network overhead
Flink committers (Maximilian Michels, Peter Vary) have agreed on the approach
Spark connector would map ROUND_ROBIN to Distributions.unspecified()

initiatives.title: Adding non-distributed actions implementation

Local implementation could be faster and more resource-efficient for small tables
Use cases include CLI tooling, CI/CD automation, REST catalog backends, and environments without distributed compute
Acknowledges scalability limitations but argues distributed computing isn't always necessary

initiatives.title: Transaction.abortTransaction API exposure
initiatives.summary: Discussion on whether to expose transaction abort functionality in Iceberg's public API. The Hive project needs to revert partial changes when multi-table transactions fail to acquire locks, currently handled by BaseTransaction.cleanUpOnCommitFailure. Proposal is to add a public Transaction.abortTransaction() method instead of just making the cleanup method protected.
key_points: Hive team needs to clean up partial changes on transaction lock acquisition failure
Current cleanup handled by BaseTransaction.cleanUpOnCommitFailure
Two options: make method protected or expose new public abortTransaction() method
Public API approach is more explicit and natural for explicit rollback scenarios

Establishing governance guidelines for AI-generated contributions as part of broader project management improvements

Refactor scattered Spark configuration management to centralize and deduplicate parsing logic
Address inconsistent configuration precedence order between read and write operations
Manage scope and coordination to minimize disruption to ongoing development and forks

Aligns specification with actual server implementation

initiatives.title: Add assert-last-sequence-number requirement to REST API
initiatives.summary: Proposal to add a new assert-last-sequence-number update requirement to the Iceberg REST API spec to handle concurrent commits. This requirement would validate that the table's sequence number hasn't advanced past the snapshot being committed, converting non-retryable ValidationException errors into retryable CommitFailedException errors in concurrent scenarios.
key_points: Concurrent REST catalog commits can cause non-retryable ValidationException due to sequence number conflicts
New assert-last-sequence-number requirement would validate sequence number state before snapshot commit
Converts sequence number conflicts into retryable CommitFailedException for automatic retry capability
Requirement would be automatically added when committing new snapshots

initiatives.title: Flink unaligned checkpoints duplicate data bug fix
initiatives.summary: A bug in Flink Sink with CDC writes can cause duplicate data when failures occur during checkpoints with unaligned checkpointing enabled. The proposed fix requires wrapping WriteResult to assign checkpointId immediately, which would break upgrading Flink jobs using unaligned checkpoints. The discussion seeks community feedback on the prevalence of unaligned checkpointing usage before proceeding.

Equality delete records in subsequent checkpoints fail to apply to data files from previous checkpoints, causing duplication
Fix requires wrapping WriteResult object to communicate checkpointId between writer and committer
